caption: Figure 1: Which patch (left or right) is 'closer' to the middle patch in these examples? In each case, the traditional metrics (L2/PSNR, SSIM, FSIM) disagree with human judgments. But deep networks, even across architectures (Squeezenet [20], AlexNet [27], VGG [52]) and supervision type (supervised [47], self-supervised [13, 40, 43, 64], and even unsupervised [26]), provide an emergent embedding which agrees surprisingly well with humans. We further calibrate existing deep embeddings on a large-scale database of perceptual judgments; models and data can be found at https://www.github.com/richzhang/PerceptualSimilarity .
description:
Figure Description: This figure presents a comparative analysis of different image similarity metrics, including traditional metrics (L2/PSNR, SSIM, FSIM) and various deep learning networks (random, unsupervised, self-supervised, supervised). Each row shows three images: a reference image, a patch to be compared, and another patch. The figure asks viewers to determine which patch is closer to the reference image. The results indicate that traditional metrics often disagree with human judgments, while deep learning networks, regardless of their architecture or training method, align more closely with human perception.
